moat_against: No switching costs or recurring revenue — fashion heat is re-earned every season
Single-brand concentration: Coach ~86% of revenue, Kate Spade shrinking post-impairment
Aspirational-consumer cyclicality: the customer trades down first in a downturn
Tariff exposure on imported leather goods; FY2027 neutrality is guidance, not a guarantee
moat_for: Coach pricing power: mid-teens handbag AUR gains with units still growing, margin expansion
Direct-to-consumer distribution control protects price integrity
Scale in accessible luxury: top-three handbag position in North America and Greater China
Gen Z customer flywheel: 11M new customers added in FY2026
moat_justification: Coach has demonstrated real pricing power (handbag AUR up mid-teens in Q4 FY2026, gross margin expansion, 23.4% non-GAAP operating margin in FY2026) and is gaining share with Gen Z customers (11M new customers added in FY2026), with direct-to-consumer control protecting price integrity — but this is a fashion brand moat with no switching costs, no recurring revenue and no structural cost advantage, and the portfolio around it is shrinking: Coach is ~86% of revenue while Kate Spade declines after a ~$855M FY2025 impairment, with tariff exposure and an aspirational, cyclical customer against it.
